content: The delayed-release capsule is indicated for the treatment of Helicobacter pylori infection in adults. The recommended dosage is four capsules taken orally three times daily, with each dose spaced at least four hours apart (e.g., morning, mid-day, and evening). The capsules should be taken with food for a duration of 14 days. Each dose contains 1000 mg of amoxicillin, 40 mg of omeprazole, and 50 mg of rifabutin. Use of this medication should be avoided in patients with severe renal impairment (glomerular filtration rate <30 mL/min) or hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class A, B, or C). To minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and maintain treatment efficacy, culture and susceptibility testing should be performed whenever possible to guide appropriate therapy. The safety and efficacy of this treatment have not been established in certain populations. Omeprazole decreases the levels of erlotinib due to its effect on gastric pH, and concomitant use of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) with erlotinib should be avoided. Drugs that alter the pH of the upper gastrointestinal tract may reduce the solubility and bioavailability of erlotinib. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to mavacamten, potentially leading to heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. Concomitant use is contraindicated. Omeprazole decreases the levels of nelfinavir through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Co-administration may result in loss of nelfinavir virologic response and resistance development, likely due to CYP2C19 inhibition of nelfinavir conversion to its active M8 metabolite and reduced gastric pH affecting nelfinavir absorption. Concomitant use is contraindicated. Omeprazole decreases the levels of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Concurrent use may lead to treatment failure and/or resistance to rilpivirine or NNRTIs due to reduced drug levels. Concomitant use is contraindicated. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of abrocitinib by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Abrocitinib is a substrate of CYP2C9 and CYP2C19. Moderate-to-strong inhibitors of these enzymes increase systemic exposure to abrocitinib and its active metabolites, potentially increasing adverse effects. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole decreases the levels of acalabrutinib by increasing gastric pH. Acalabrutinib solubility decreases as gastric pH increases. Due to the prolonged effect of PPIs, separating doses may not eliminate the interaction. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Co-administration of apalutamide, a strong CYP2C19 inducer, with CYP2C19 substrates can result in lower exposure to these medications. Alternative drugs should be used when possible. Omeprazole decreases the levels of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to substantially reduced plasma concentrations when co-administered with PPIs. PPI doses should not exceed omeprazole 20 mg and must be taken approximately 12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naive patients. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole decreases the effects of ceritinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole decreases the effects of clopidogrel by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Clopidogrel efficacy may be reduced by drugs that inhibit CYP2C19, as its antiplatelet activity depends on an active metabolite formed via CYP2C19 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of dacomitinib through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Concomitant use with a PPI decreases dacomitinib concentrations, potentially reducing its efficacy. PPIs should be avoided with dacomitinib. Locally-acting antacids or H2-receptor antagonists may be used as alternatives. Omeprazole decreases the levels of dasatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of digoxin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of fedratinib through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Concomitant use of fedratinib, a CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 substrate, with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors should be avoided. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole decreases the levels of indinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole decreases the levels of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole decreases the levels of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole decreases the levels of levoketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Lonafarnib increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole decreases the effects of mesalamine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and applies specifically to sustained-release dosage forms. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole decreases the levels of neratinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole decreases the levels of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. Nilotinib has pH-dependent solubility, and separating doses may not eliminate this effect due to the extended duration of PPI action. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole decreases the levels of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole may cause a hyperresponse in gastrin secretion during stimulation testing with secretin, falsely suggesting gastrinoma. Temporarily stop omeprazole treatment at least 14 days before assessing gastrin levels to allow them to return to baseline. Omeprazole decreases the levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. Velpatasvir solubility decreases as gastric pH increases, becoming practically insoluble at pH >5. Concomitant use is not recommended. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of sotorasib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole decreases the effects of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of abrocitinib by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Omeprazole decreases the levels of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor patients. Armodafinil increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Omeprazole increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of belumosudil by increasing gastric pH. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of belzutifan by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. Bortezomib increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Omeprazole decreases the levels of bosutinib by approximately 45% due to its pH-dependent solubility. Use caution and monitor patients. Omeprazole decreases the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored.
